body:
## Problem and result

When DeepSeek V4.1's experts do not fit in VRAM and RAM, many of the experts a token needs are read from the SSD, and decode and prompt reads wait for them. On a 12 GB laptop, decode spends 83 of its 198 ms a token on 30 store misses.

With `STRATA_DS4_CACHE_ROUTE=<ram>[,<vram>]` set, the router's selection bias gives a bonus to the experts the RAM store or VRAM hold. A near tie then goes to an expert that needs no SSD read. On the same laptop, `0.2,0.3` writes 10.9 tok/s instead of 7.0 and reads seven agent turns in 55 s instead of 109 s. In return, the top-1 token matches the unchanged engine at 93.2% of positions and perplexity rises 0.5%. When the variable is unset, every route is as before.

## Related discussion

#4936. @PhialsBasement measured the same idea as `DS4_TIE_PEN` (a penalty for the experts not held) on HIP gfx1201 and suggested this standalone opt-in PR: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/4936#issuecomment-6714468448. The idea and the two-tier form (VRAM ahead of RAM) are theirs. A maintainer has not agreed on the scope yet. The change is opt-in and leaves every default as it is.

## Approach

DeepSeek already selects experts with a selection-only bias: the top-k is picked from `score + gate.bias`, and the mixing weights come from `score` alone. This change keeps a second copy of `gate.bias` per layer on the device. That copy holds `gate.bias + <vram>` for an expert in a VRAM slot, `gate.bias + <ram>` for one in the RAM store, and `gate.bias` for every other expert. The three routing call sites (prompt chunks, async decode, sync decode) read that copy instead of `gate.bias`.

The weights are untouched, so a substituted expert counts with its own router weight. A bonus for the held experts and a penalty of the same size for the others pick the same top-k. `0.2,0.3` here is therefore `DS4_TIE_PEN=0.3` plus `DS4_TIE_PEN_RAM=0.1` on the fork branch.

The copy is rebuilt from the CPU before each prompt and every 16 decode steps. Each rebuild reads `slot[]`, `ram[]` and a new `ExpertStore::holds()` and copies 40 x 384 floats (61 KB) to the device. No kernel changes.

The bonus is left out in three places:
- MTP layers;
- layers split across GPUs (`nm != 1`);
- image tokens, which keep their own bias (`gate_bias_vl`).

The startup log says when the bonus is on and that it changes the answers.

Unset, `gate_bias_cr` stays null and `route_bias()` returns `gate.bias`: the default path is the release path.

Files: `src/dsv41/ds4_model.cu` (+64, -4), `src/dsv41/ds4_store.hpp` (+5), `docs/DEEPSEEK41.md` (one paragraph and a measured table under "Speed").

## Validation

Environment: Strata main 146df3c4 (engine 0.1.58) plus this branch, Windows 11, RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB (PCIe 5.0 x8), Core Ultra 9 275HX, 64 GB DDR5-5600, NVMe at 4.7 GB/s (1 MiB random reads), ISTA-DAS 2.00 bpw, Faster (5 experts). In the runs, 282 to 322 experts are in VRAM and about 3,400 in the RAM store.

**Passed:**

- Build: CUDA 13.0, MSVC 2022, sm_120, `packaging/build_dsv41_windows.bat` with `DSV41_ARCH=120-real`. No new compiler warnings (the same 17 warning lines as main).
- Off is byte-identical: `strata-dsv41 --pack PACK --max-context 8192 --dspark auto --vision off --profile-readonly --score set.ids.json --score-out RUN.tsv`. The ids are `data/quant_quality/v1` tokenized with the pack's tokenizer, 4,995 positions. The TSV of this branch with the variable unset has the same SHA-256 as the release engine 0.1.58's, and two runs of the release engine give the same bytes.
- Quality: the same `--score` command with the variable set, then `python tools/quant_quality.py compare OFF.tsv RUN.tsv --segments`, against this branch unset:

  | `STRATA_DS4_CACHE_ROUTE` | top-1 | KL | KL p99 | PPL (unset: 3.173) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 0.05 | 95.8% | 0.0125 | 0.121 | 3.177 |
  | 0.1 | 95.4% | 0.0161 | 0.146 | 3.178 |
  | 0.2 | 94.4% | 0.0232 | 0.227 | 3.177 |
  | 0.2,0.3 | 93.2% | 0.0271 | 0.244 | 3.189 |
  | 0.3 | 92.9% | 0.0314 | 0.279 | 3.207 |
  | 0.4 | 92.1% | 0.0397 | 0.369 | 3.259 |

  For scale, Faster (5 experts) against Full (6) on the same set: KL 0.0172. By segment at `0.2,0.3`, English and docs move most (KL 0.036 and 0.045), while code and the agent transcript move least (0.015 and 0.018).
- Decode, CLI: `strata-dsv41 --pack PACK --ids @prompt4k.ids --n 256 --max-context 131072 --vision on --reserve-mib 900 --profile-readonly`, with `DS4_LANE_CAL=none DS4_NO_EOS=1`. The prompt is 4,000 tokens. Three runs each, round-robin, the same day:

  | setting | tok/s (runs) | store misses a token | SSD MB a token |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | unset | 7.02 (6.94, 7.14, 6.99) | 29.2 | 252 |
  | 0.2 | 10.21 (10.39, 10.00, 10.25) | 14.2 | 124 |
  | 0.3 | 10.56 (9.80, 10.93, 10.95) | 12.1 | 106 |
  | 0.2,0.3 | 10.87 (10.72, 10.90, 10.99) | 13.5 | 118 |

  `0.2,0.3` misses the store more often than `0.3` but is faster: it moves near ties to the VRAM experts, and the CPU lane's time per token falls from about 77 to 70 ms.
- Agent turns, `--serve`, two runs each, round-robin, with `STRATA_DS4_SLOT_KEEP=0 DS4_LANE_CAL=none`:
  - one model load, a 4,000-token base prompt;
  - seven turns that each append 16, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1,024 and 2,048 tokens of repository files to the previous prompt, with 8 greedy tokens each;
  - 256 greedy tokens at the end.

  | setting | prompt reads of the 7 turns | last answer |
  |---|---|---|
  | unset | 108.5 s (105.3, 111.6) | 7.6 tok/s (6.95, 8.28) |
  | 0.2 | 60.1 s (59.9, 60.3) | 12.0 tok/s (10.82, 13.16) |
  | 0.3 | 52.7 s (52.4, 53.0) | 15.3 tok/s (14.74, 15.94) |
  | 0.2,0.3 | 55.2 s (55.1, 55.4) | 15.7 tok/s (15.71, 15.75) |

  The benchmark is a small Python script that drives the serve protocol, and I can attach it.
- App: the release app's `serve.server` with this engine and `STRATA_DS4_CACHE_ROUTE` set started and answered a chat request, and the startup log line was printed.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**

- HIP and Metal builds. Both compile `ds4_model.cu`. The new code calls only functions the file already calls (`cudaMalloc`, `cudaMemcpy`, `cudaGetDevice`, `cudaSetDevice`, `std::getenv`, `std::atof`, `std::strchr`). That it builds there is unconfirmed static analysis. A HIP build on gfx1201 would cover the hardware @PhialsBasement measured. I am keeping this PR as a draft until then, and I would welcome a HIP or Metal build from anyone who has one.
- Multi-GPU: layers split across GPUs keep plain routing, but this was not run with two cards.
- `--parallel`, vision requests, Full (6 experts) speed, `--score` above an 8K context, and task-level quality (coding suites, long answers).
- Long agent sessions. The Qwen engine's `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR` is the same idea, and at 1.5 it was taken back as a default because of repetition loops in long agent sessions and fewer agent tasks solved (#4402: perplexity +22.9% at 1.5 and +1.1% at 0.5 on an RTX 4070 Ti, IQ3_XXS). Here `0.2,0.3` costs +0.5% perplexity on a short set, but no session past 16K tokens was run with it, so whether it loops there is not known.

## Limits

- The answers depend on which experts the caches hold, so a prompt's answer depends on what ran before it and can differ between runs.
- The biased rows are up to 16 decode steps old.
- There is no automatic value: the bonus is a quality-for-speed trade the user picks.
title: [Engine] dsv41: STRATA_DS4_CACHE_ROUTE, a selection bonus for the experts VRAM or the RAM store already hold (opt-in, changes the answers)
